advances: A conditional cap-cover criterion. The lower bound on the selected cap budget controls source depth when the caps attain that depth.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Set $a=|A|$, $k=|K|$, $r_i=|R_i|$, $\kappa=\sum_i r_i/a$ and let $q_i$ be the middle trace volume. Since the $B$ capture vanishes, $q_i+a-r_i\le Q$. If $Q\ge a$, apply the ordinary $d$-volume specialization of the hereditary cap-trimming bound ac7ba1e1e0ebc955 to the closed middle traces, with $\alpha=Q-a$. They are halfspaces with nonzero normals that cover $K$. Since $(q_i-\alpha)_+\le r_i$, the bound gives $k\le\kappa a+(Q-a)/\Gamma_d$, or $Q\ge\Gamma_d k+(1-\Gamma_d\kappa)a$. In the disjoint case $\kappa\le1\le1/\Gamma_d-1$ since the binomial theorem gives $(1+1/d)^d\ge2$. The same upper bound on $\kappa$ is stipulated in the second case. Both give the claimed budget.

If $Q<a$, the cover sum gives $k\le\sum_iq_i\le m(Q-a)+\kappa a$, hence $k<\kappa a$ and $Q\ge[k+(m-\kappa)a]/m$. Both hypotheses imply $\kappa\le m-1$, using $m\ge2$ in the disjoint case and $m\ge1/\Gamma_d$ in the other. For $x\ge0$, the derivative of $(x+m-\kappa)/(m(x+1))$ has the sign of $\kappa-(m-1)$. Thus, at $x=k/a<\kappa$, the ratio is at least its value $1/(1+\kappa)$ at $x=\kappa$. The latter is at least $\Gamma_d$ by the same upper bound on $\kappa$, which proves the budget in this case as well. If $\kappa=0$, $k<\kappa a$ is impossible. For the count assertion, $\Gamma_d\ge1/(d+1)$ is equivalent to $(1+1/d)^{d-1}\le d$. This is immediate for $d=1,2$, and for $d\ge3$ the left side is less than $e<3\le d$. For $d=2$, $1/\Gamma_2-1=5/4$.

If $B$ is nonheavy then $a+k\ge M/2$. If $B$ is heavy, apply the full-mass case of 6769574fc1bd9f8d in $B$, which is the usual centroid bound. A closed containing halfspace has either a containing continuous halfspace trace on the fiber or the entire fiber when the continuous normal vanishes. The $B$ contribution alone is at least $\Gamma_d|B|>\Gamma_d M/2$.

statement:
Let $A,K,B$ be $d$-dimensional convex bodies at integer bases $-1,0,1$, $d\ge1$, with mixed measure the sum of their $d$-volumes. Suppose $m\ge2$ closed ambient halfspaces with nonzero continuous normals cover $K$ by their middle traces, capture zero volume on $B$, and each capture total mixed volume at most $Q$. Let $R_i$ be the strict uncaptured subset of $A$ for halfspace $i$, and write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Then $Q\ge\Gamma_d(|A|+|K|)$ if the $R_i$ are pairwise disjoint up to volume zero. The same conclusion holds if $m\ge1/\Gamma_d$ and $\sum_i|R_i|\le(1/\Gamma_d-1)|A|$. The count $m=d+1$ suffices in this second case, with allowance $5|A|/4$ in the plane.

Writing $M=|A|+|K|+|B|$, if $|B|\le|A|+|K|$ either condition yields $Q\ge\Gamma_d M/2$. If $|B|>|A|+|K|$, the ordinary centroid in the actual fiber $B$ has raw mixed depth strictly greater than $\Gamma_d M/2$.
title: Disjoint or bounded residuals certify a three-fiber cap-cover budget
